text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000086 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity stratum, but the few returned charts support the billed levels and are too thin to settle whether this is upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess is not confined to sick patients: the 99215 share runs above the all-provider rate even for patients with 0 or 1 conditions, and the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include routine-looking presentations such as upper respiratory infection (C0049062, C0049251), rash (C0049524, C0050226) and follow-up-only visits (C0050139). That pattern is consistent with upcoding, but the heavy 99214 mix and the steep rise in 99215 share with condition count also fit a practice that codes high across a genuinely complex panel. The documentation does not resolve this: only 3 documented 99215 claims came back (C0049632, C0049778, C0049985, all supported at high MDM), records cover a very small share of claims, and the few notes claiming moderate-plus data review without a lab or test line are only weak evidence of inflated notes. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims (for example C0048590, C0049062, C0050139, C0050382) to see whether high MDM is genuinely documented for single-complaint visits. They should also check those notes for cloned or templated language."}
